metric_rationale: This metric calculates the proportion of choices that align with the Take The Best (TTB) prediction. The experimental design strongly dissociates TTB from Tallying: out of 8 trial types, TTB and Tallying make strictly opposite predictions on 6 of them, and Tallying predicts a tie on the remaining 2. Consequently, data generated by the TTB theory will yield a metric value close to 1.0, while data generated by the Tallying theory will yield a value close to 0.125 (since it systematically chooses the opposite option on 75% of trials and guesses on the rest). This massive mean difference, combined with the low per-subject variance over 96 trials, guarantees a highly significant discrimination.

This metric calculates the proportion of choices that align with the strict prediction of the Tallying heuristic, on trials where Tallying makes a strict prediction (i.e., no ties). Because the experimental design deliberately pits Tallying against Take The Best (TTB) such that they often make diametrically opposite predictions, this metric will yield a high value under the Tallying theory and a very low value under TTB, providing a clean and highly discriminative contrast.
